The Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation yields a nonlinear PDE for the value function J(π,t). By eliminating J, the optimal strategy α(π,t) satisfies a self-contained PDE, which is a backward parabolic diffusion equation. This PDE is solved numerically via explicit Euler scheme with stability condition Δθ/(Δz)² < 0.5. In the long-run limit, the solution converges to u(z,θ) → 1 - z, indicating that risk exposure decays linearly with distance to stop. The boundary conditions define α(πc,t) = 0 (stop-hit), α(π,T) = αK (terminal), and α → αK as π → ∞. These conditions ensure that the strategy respects both terminal and stop-loss constraints. The derived scaling factor u(z,θ) provides a principled method for dynamically adjusting stake size in response to risk exposure and time to reset. This framework directly enables GSE to manage risk-sensitive bankroll allocation while maintaining optimality under the Kelly criterion.
